evidence.claim: Black Rock Coffee Bar described itself as a fast-growing, fully company-owned, drive-thru-led specialty coffee platform with 181 locations across seven states as of December 31, 2025.
evidence.source_title: Black Rock Coffee Bar details growth and 2025 IPO | BRCB Annual Report (10-K)

evidence.claim: Black Rock Coffee Bar reported that proprietary Fuel energy drinks generated about 24% of 2025 revenue and loyalty accounted for roughly 63% of 2025 sales, supporting beverage mix, loyalty, and mobile-ordering as important restaurant operating nodes.
evidence.source_title: Black Rock Coffee Bar details growth and 2025 IPO | BRCB Annual Report (10-K)

evidence.claim: Black Rock Coffee Bar highlighted risks around rapid store growth execution, supply chain, labor, leverage, the Tax Receivable Agreement, and multi-class governance, supporting capital access and execution as restaurant growth bottlenecks.
evidence.source_title: Black Rock Coffee Bar details growth and 2025 IPO | BRCB Annual Report (10-K)

evidence.claim: Reborn Coffee announced a strategic distribution partnership with Sysco intended to support nationwide franchise expansion through distribution network access, ordering infrastructure, service capabilities, quality assurance, food-safety protocols, and local sourcing support.
evidence.source_title: Reborn Coffee Announces Strategic Distribution Partnership with Sysco to Support National Franchise Expansion

evidence.claim: Sysco was described in the Reborn Coffee announcement as a global leader in selling, marketing, and distributing food and related products, making it a reference-scale foodservice distribution node.
evidence.source_title: Reborn Coffee Announces Strategic Distribution Partnership with Sysco to Support National Franchise Expansion

evidence.claim: A recent Wingstop analysis described franchisee economics with estimated build costs of $575,000 to $650,000, roughly $2 million in annual sales, and 22% to 25% restaurant-level profit margins, framing unit economics as a central restaurant growth driver.

The same Wingstop analysis stated that Wingstop shifted most system wing purchases from spot-market exposure into contracted pricing beginning in 2024, illustrating procurement structure as a franchisee-margin bottleneck.

The Fore Coffee IPO analysis framed app-based ordering, loyalty, digital payments, pickup workflows, delivery commission exposure, and data-driven repeat behavior as important modern food-and-beverage operating levers.
evidence.source_title: Inside Fore Coffee IPO: A Financial Breakdown

evidence.claim: Fast-casual restaurant operators increasingly depend on supply-chain resilience for availability, cost control, and brand trust, which supports the relevance of foodservice distribution, procurement, QA, and fulfillment reliability nodes.
evidence.source_title: Why Supply Chain Resilience Now Defines the Survival of Fast Casual | Modern Restaurant Management

memory_update.text: DIN maps primarily to the franchise royalty/ad-fund node rather than direct restaurant traffic alone; survival in later layers depends on franchisee returns, remodel burden, ad fund health, and net unit stability.

WEST is a potentially underfollowed B2B beverage supply-chain candidate, but the restaurant exposure is still a hypothesis until named customers, foodservice channel materiality, capacity utilization, and coffee-cost pass-through are verified.
NATH should be mapped as a hybrid brand-licensing, foodservice branded-products, and small franchisor relationship, not as a standard restaurant operator.
WEN is a reference-scale but still non-mega-cap QSR franchisor where the key Serenity variable is franchisee health and development economics, not headline same-store sales alone.

MIDD is a second-order restaurant capex supplier linked to remodels, new-unit builds, kitchen throughput, and labor-saving equipment; relationship remains unproven without restaurant-customer and order/backlog evidence.

RAVE and FARM are speculative shadow candidates below the preferred market-cap range; they require liquidity, reporting-quality, and business-stability checks before promotion to later Serenity layers.
TOST is included as a reference leader for restaurant POS/payments/software architecture and should not crowd out smaller restaurant technology candidates such as PAR.
PAR maps to enterprise restaurant POS, loyalty, and back-office software; key verification items are named enterprise customers, ARR mix, churn, implementation backlog, and module attach rates.

Primary-source filings are needed for all tickers in this candidate chunk; current Layer 2B relationships rely heavily on cached Layer 1 context and external thematic evidence rather than direct company filing extraction.
The highest-priority next evidence pass should quantify restaurant-channel materiality and customer concentration for WEST, FARM, THS, MIDD, PAR, and TOST.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into restaurant-theme ticker relationships across franchisor royalty systems, foodservice and beverage supply chains, restaurant equipment/remodel infrastructure, and restaurant software/POS/payments. Stronger current evidence supports the franchisor/royalty candidates DIN, NATH, WEN, and RAVE at the relationship level from cached Layer 1 context, while WEST, FARM, THS, MIDD, TOST, and PAR remain mainly hypothesis/inference relationships pending primary filings, customer disclosures, and segment materiality checks. The highest Serenity-style underfollowed angles are not simply restaurant traffic, but franchisee unit economics, supplier incentive/royalty durability, private-label beverage procurement, commercial kitchen capex, and restaurant operating software adoption.
